operation.body:
### Goal

Demonstrate that feedback data survives a real process restart (FR-005): created items and category changes remain available after stopping and starting the Rails app against the same SQLite database file.

### Acceptance criteria

- Automated test (or documented repeatable check integrated into the test suite) proves persistence across a real process boundary using the same file-backed database—not merely clearing an in-memory/query cache.
- Evidence covers at least one created feedback item and one category change surviving restart.
- README or test comments state how to run the persistence check locally; report only checks that actually ran in CI.
- Pull request contains exact `Closes #<this-issue-number>` and stays within FR-005 scope.
- No regression to FR-001–FR-004 flows covered by existing controller/model tests.

### Constraints

- Ruby on Rails, SQLite, server-rendered HTML; MIT license; no authentication.
- Build on current `main` at `6f2ff08` (goals #4/#9/#11/#13/#15 merged).
- Do not edit `docs/security-review.md` or implement goal #3 work.
- Keep CI economical; prefer a focused automated boundary test over broad refactors.

### Out of scope

- Broad invalid-request handling (FR-006), full FR-007 gap-fill beyond persistence boundary, FR-008 documentation sweep, sample dataset seeding, and demo recording.

### Relevant context

SQLite lives under `storage/` per stack profile. FR-001–FR-004 behaviour is on `main`. Parent project #2 targets FR-001–FR-008 overall.
